terms.gloss: an automaton, a machine that moves by itself
evidence: Suet. Claud. 34.2: sī automatum vel pēgma vel quid tāle aliud parum cessisset
M-O s.v. machine: automatum, i n.
terms.comment: Greek αὐτόματον, “self-moving”, with every vowel short; Lewis & Short also gives the Greek form automaton. Classically a mechanical figure or a stage device that works by itself. Modern Latin also uses it of a motor vehicle (Bacci’s automatum longum, a bus, M-O s.v. bus), and Morgan–Owens of any machine; for a robot see robot. The adjective is automatus, self-moving (Petr. 50.1, Lewis & Short), and a maker of automata is an automatārius (an inscription, Lewis & Short).
